title: Matthew
tagline: Jesus as the king Israel was waiting for, told for readers who knew Israel's Scriptures well.
author: Traditionally Matthew
authorNote: The book doesn't name its author. Church tradition from the second century credits Matthew, the tax collector who became one of the twelve. Many scholars question this.
audienceNote: Most likely a community of Jewish believers, perhaps in Syria (Antioch is often suggested), working out where they stood with the synagogue.
settingNote: Herod the Great, then his sons, ruled for Rome. Judea later came under a Roman governor. Hopes for a coming king ran high.
genreNote: An ancient biography with a purpose. Watch the five long teaching sections and the many "this was to fulfill" quotations.
bigIdea: Jesus is the king Israel was waiting for, and his kingdom (*basileia*) is arriving in ways no one expected.
mapSummary: The story starts in Bethlehem, detours to Egypt, settles in Galilee around the lake, then turns south to Jerusalem.

scene.author: Traditionally Matthew
scene.happening: Roman rule in Judea and Galilee
